explanation: Fires retrospectively at the boundary token that opens the next segment of an already-established multi-segment run - the digit of a numbered item marker (' 5', '6.'), the bullet that starts the next line, or the period-plus-line-break / blank line that ends a paragraph line - with strength equal to a running count of same-format segments: essentially zero at the run's first marker, about 0.1 of max at the second, 0.2-0.3 at the third, 0.3-0.4 at the fourth, 0.4-0.6 at the fifth to seventh, and 0.45-0.75 of max (up to the scan maximum) at the sixth to tenth line of a long multi-line document; measured 0.00/0.18/0.47/0.56/0.68 of activation on the five numbered items '3.'-'7.' of a workshop notice, 0.08/0.29/0.37/0.53/1.01 on a volunteer handbook list, and 0.28/0.47/0.44/0.39/0.73 across the paragraph breaks of a narrative. Without such a run it stays at or just below the 0.25 active line: a lone marker or break inside running prose, a two-item list, a run whose items merely repeat one line, and lists of bare numerals or measurements do not accumulate, while inserting one prose sentence between two items does not reset an established run.
